messages:
incident-bot: Pager: Elevated 5xx + high latency seen in us-east-1 for Hosted API and Dedicated pools. Source: increased STS/KMS error rate and observability egress errors. Paging oncall.
maria (oncall): I’m on it. seeing spikes in 5xx ~ 15m. Dashboard: hosted-api latency 1200ms p95, dedicated-pool-03 returning 503 on inference path.
kevin: Confirmed. Graphs show STS token refresh failures from control-plane -> sts.amazonaws.com, and our LogShipper vendor returning 502s on their ingest endpoint. Could be multi-vector.
alex (infra): I’m checking egress and NAT host conntrack counts. `kubectl get pods -n controlplane` looks ok. Opening AWS support thread just in case.
emily (support): Heads up — we have customers hitting retries. Notified two paying customers (acct: BrightMetrics, PsiWare) with brief note. Will update with severity.
sam (sre): Dumping recent proxy logs for one of the failed requests: ``[2026-03-17T18:03:12Z] proxy: upstream sts.amazonaws.com 504 timeout, attempt=3 token_refresh``. Also seeing errors from logshipper: `POST https://ingest.logshipper.example 502`.
maria (oncall): Immediate mitigation ideas: 1) throttle/queue non-essential observability egress (lower retention batch), 2) route Hosted API read-only traffic to eu-west-1 fallback for latency-sensitive customers, 3) scale dedicated pools away from affected nodes if NAT saturation.
kevin: Agree. I can flip egress reducer for LogShipper (disable real-time forwarder) — reduces STS tokens churn too since some exporters create temporary creds.
alex (infra): Starting cookbook: `infra run disable-logshipper-forwarding --region us-east-1` now. Also bumping nat-gw autoscaling to add more egress IPs.
ops-bot: Action logged: disable-logshipper-forwarding triggered by alex at 18:06 UTC. Task id: TG-8842.
emily (support): Notifying customers that we have degraded write observability and increased retrying, not affecting persisted outputs. Will post to status page: "Elevated latency and error rates in US-EAST-1 affecting API calls and metrics ingestion."
sam (sre): After disabling forwarder, I see immediate reduction in outbound 502s. STS token error rate down ~60% in the last 4 mins. p95 latency trending down to ~700ms.
maria (oncall): Good. Next: run canary fallback for hosted-api region routing for heavy-latency routes. kevin, can you push a route-rule to send 5% traffic to eu-west-1?
kevin: Pushing canary rule now: `routeset apply --name us-east-fallback-5pct --match header:x-region-priority=low --route eu-west-1`. Done. Monitoring logs.
alex (infra): NAT conntrack freed up after scale out. Still watching control-plane kube-proxy for retransmits.
sam (sre): Canary looks healthy so far. 5% routed, errors in eu-west are fine. p95 for canary ~120ms.
emily (support): Updating customers: added ETA 1h, mitigations in progress, will post every 30m or on major change.
maria (oncall): Paging handoff in 45m to kevin. I'll stay until handoff unless major regression. Anyone else want to take secondary?
kevin: I can take next oncall handoff. Will also keep AWS support thread open: ticket 12345-REDWOOD.
alex (infra): Added a temporary fallback to reuse older cached STS creds for control plane auth where safe: `auth-cache-ttl=300`. This reduces new STS calls.
sam (sre): Observability: disabling non-critical metric exports reduced egress by ~40%. Request queueing also reduced 503 tail.
incident-bot: Incident updated: severity=high -> mitigation_in_progress. Tags: aws, sts, observability, us-east-1.
emily (support): Logged customer impact notes: "API request latency increased; some requests returned 5xx. Dedicated pools in us-east-1 experienced intermittent 503s. We applied egress controls and partial region fallback."
maria (oncall): If things stabilize in next 30m, we'll move to recovery mode and craft postmortem owner. If not, we escalate to exec communications.
kevin: For follow-ups: create internal ticket to evaluate LogShipper retry/backoff and our STS token usage patterns. We should also add circuit-breaker around third-party ingestion.
alex (infra): AWS support responded: "Investigating elevated STS errors in us-east-1; no broader regional outage noted yet." Keeping thread.
sam (sre): Last check: request 5xx rate down 70%, p95 ~420ms. Dedicated pool errors largely gone. Continuing watch.
emily (support): Status page updated. Sending proactive DM to top affected customers.
maria (oncall): Thanks all. Handoff to kevin at 18:51 UTC. If anyone sees new 5xx spike, ping @maria or @kevin immediately. :thumbsup:
